title: Ink Storm
tagline: Stir a river of glowing ink and see which method keeps its detail.

paper.title: A neural characteristic mapping method: Lagrangian PINNs based on flow maps for transport-dominated problems

novelty: No known implementation (not verified): a live interactive comparison pairs ordinary dye advection with classical characteristic-map pullback in a shared procedural flow.
description: A browser fluid artwork that compares how repeated grid sampling smears dye while carrying a flow map preserves fine initial pattern detail.
howItWorks: A WebGL2 shader advects both the dye and a backward characteristic map through the same analytic swirling velocity field. The left half repeatedly samples dye; the right half samples the original pattern through the composed map. The paper uses neural networks to learn flow maps; this demo uses a simplified classical map technique and no learned model.
controls: Drag the artwork to stir and drag the center handle to move the comparison. Double-tap or double-click to add a vortex impulse. Use Reset, Pattern to cycle three initial images, and Split view to switch to a full-frame view.
